prize_parts.citation: For establishing liquid-liquid phase separation, through the liquid behaviour of P granules and the multivalent phase transition of signalling proteins, as a physical-chemical principle by which biomolecules organise into membraneless compartments

statement.case_for: I keep biomolecular condensation as my preferred single-part prize. The round-1 exchange did not weaken the core scientific claim: multivalent weak interactions drive demixing, and the resulting compartments are described by phase diagrams, valency, interfacial tension and material state. Hyman and Brangwynne (P granules as liquids, 2009) and Rosen (multivalent proteins undergoing a sharp, quantitatively described transition, 2012) are the founding experiments, reproduced in many laboratories and reconstituted in vitro with controlled components. The chair's question is whether a citation can reward the principle without endorsing contested cellular condensates. I think it can, by crediting the physical principle and the founding experiments only, which is how I have worded the citation. This is physical chemistry of self-assembly applied to the cell, a new concept of molecular organisation, and I believe chemistry should recognise it.
statement.case_against: My candidate has the narrowest support among the leading positions: I am its only explicit supporter, and only four members ranked it at all. The in vivo debate is real, since overexpression, crowding and loose use of the word condensate mean some claims will not survive, and a prize can freeze a contested framing. Credit is also unresolved, because Pappu and Mittag supplied much of the sequence-grammar and thermodynamic framework that three names cannot cover. Round 1 also showed that B007 and B011 are each backed by more members and are better known to a general audience. I give that real weight, but I do not treat support counts as a measure of scientific merit, and I have not found an argument that moves my own ranking.

responses.point: Johan argues that targeted protein degradation (B011) is the only candidate every member ranked, and that this breadth matters more than first-place votes, with a coherent Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli attribution.
responses.response: I rank B011 fifth and it is my first alternative, so I take the breadth argument seriously, and your attribution is cleaner than I first thought. But I read breadth of ranking as acceptance, as Daniel does, not as merit, since the same breadth could be produced by a candidate nobody objects to rather than one anyone champions. The two concerns that remain for me are ones you share: no approved degrader, and a citation that would sit beside, without crediting, Handa, Ito and Gray. If the committee converges on B011, I could support your three names, and I would prefer a citation worded around induced proximity and E3 ligase recruitment so that the cereblon glue work is not implicitly dismissed.

responses.point: Heiner holds that base editing is a distinct invention from the 2020 cutting tools, explainable to a general audience, with the tractable Liu, Komor and Gaudelli attribution, and that phase separation is somewhat premature.
responses.response: Your argument that deaminase engineering and directed evolution are distinct from CRISPR cleavage is persuasive and I have moved toward B007 as a serious option; it is not my first choice only because the 2020 prize is six years old and Target-AID remains unresolved at three names. On maturity, I disagree with the framing. The liquid behaviour of P granules and the multivalent transition are quantitatively reconstituted and repeatedly reproduced, and what is open is how many cellular assemblies behave this way, which is a question about scope, not about the principle. A narrow citation addresses exactly that concern. I would ask you to say whether a citation restricted to the physical principle would still read to you as premature.

responses.point: Peter proposes a two-part prize pairing Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) with base editing for Liu alone, for a total of three laureates, while conceding that the parts share no theme and that B065 had thin opening support.
responses.response: I appreciate the candour about B065, and C-N coupling is clearly mature and widely used. My difficulty is with the structure. Assigning Liu alone to a second part leaves out Komor and Gaudelli, who invented the two editor classes, and pairing unrelated fields to fit a three-person limit looks to me like a compromise to reach a count and not a judgment of what the most important chemical discovery is. I would rather the committee decide whether base editing deserves a full prize with its three names than split it. I also still see the 2010 cross-coupling prize as close enough to B065 that whether C-N coupling is a distinct achievement should be settled first.

responses.point: Peter argues that nitrogenase states a mechanism in physical terms but acknowledges that it is a line of work, that Dean and Ribbe are excluded, and that the N2 binding mode is unresolved.
responses.response: I agree with your own caveats: the structures are firmly established, but a citation for mechanism while the N2 binding mode is open is exposed, and the Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt split between structure and mechanism is contestable. Your honesty about holding the only first-place vote is the same position I am in with B046. The difference I would draw is that the phase separation claim at the level I cite is a statement about thermodynamic behaviour that has been quantitatively tested, whereas the nitrogenase mechanism is explicitly not closed. As a membrane physical chemist I would welcome your view on whether you regard phase behaviour as chemistry in the sense you apply to mechanism.

uncertainties: Whether colleagues will accept a cell-biology-adjacent discovery as chemistry, and whether a citation limited to the physical principle is enough to answer the maturity objection.
How to handle Pappu and Mittag relative to Rosen, since three names cannot reflect the sequence-encoded phase behaviour framework.

Whether base editing is distinct enough from the 2020 prize and tractable at three names given Target-AID, and whether the lack of an approved degrader weakens B011 enough that B007 is the better broad-support option.
Whether my narrow support means B046 cannot reach a majority, and whether I should be prepared to support B007 or B011 in the final vote.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I work in lipid and membrane physical chemistry and sit with Lund colleagues Linke and Somfai, but no shortlisted candidate is a Lund colleague or collaborator that I know of. I disclose field overlap with B046 (phase behaviour of biomolecules) and B058 (lipid nanoparticles), which I do not treat as grounds for recusal. Round 1 raised no new conflict.
